row.team_price_text: Pay-as-you-go: usage-based per product, free monthly allowance, no per-seat fee
row.evidence: SSO and 2FA enforcement, SAML, and SCIM: Enforce SSO and 2FA for the whole organization. Add SAML on Scale and SCIM provisioning on Enterprise.
row.notes: PostHog has no per-seat pricing: products are usage-priced with a free monthly allowance and unlimited team members, so team_price_per_user_mo and the multiplier are null. SSO/SCIM sit in flat-fee 'platform packages' layered on the usage bill: Boost $250/mo (SSO enforcement, JIT for Google/GitHub/GitLab logins), Scale $750/mo (SAML and OIDC SSO), Enterprise (SCIM, RBAC) listed as 'Custom pricing' on the rendered packages and enterprise pages. The machine-readable posthog.com/pricing.md lists Enterprise at $2000/mo, which conflicts with the rendered pages (see conflicts), so the numeric field is left null. SCIM needs verified authentication domains; roles are mapped by name from IdP groups. Packages are billed monthly. No PostHog app in the Okta Integration Network (catalogue search, rendered in a browser); Okta, Entra and OneLogin provisioning use the generic SCIM 2.0 endpoint.

plans.price_text: Usage-based per product above the free monthly allowance

auth.token_source: PostHog organization authentication settings > SCIM > Configure (per verified authentication domain); token can be regenerated via API

roles.how: IdP groups pushed via SCIM create or link PostHog roles (Okta 'Create Group' creates a role, 'Link Group' links an existing one); roles matched by name, case-sensitive; OneLogin maps roles via a 'Set Groups' rule

limitations.text: Email domains of provisioned users must be added and verified as PostHog authentication domains first.
Role matching is by name and case-sensitive; linking an Okta group to an existing PostHog role renames the role to match Okta.
SAML alone does not remove users; deprovisioning requires SCIM. Enabling or enforcing SAML does not disable personal API key usage.
PostHog does not charge per seat (unlimited team members), so 'frees the seat' does not apply.

user_api.base_url: https://us.posthog.com (US Cloud) or https://eu.posthog.com (EU Cloud) for private endpoints

endpoints.purpose: Partially update a membership (e.g. membership level)
Remove a member from the organization
Add a member to a role
Remove a member from a role
Organization-wide activity logs for SIEM polling (admins/owners)
SCIM request logs for a verified domain

rate_limits.text: Private CRUD endpoints: 480/minute and 4800/hour; limits apply to the entire organization (all users).

limitations.text: Members API exposes membership level and removal; no documented endpoint to deactivate (rather than remove) a member.
Personal API keys are deleted when a user is deleted.

fallbacks.other_sync: Just-in-time provisioning on first login via GitHub, GitLab, Google or SAML for verified domains (Boost and above)

conflicts.text: The machine-readable posthog.com/pricing.md lists the Enterprise package at $2000/mo, while the rendered platform-packages page shows Enterprise as Custom pricing; the numeric price is left null.

searched: OneLogin connector page for PostHog (bot protection, not loaded)
open_questions: Docs do not say whether SAML/OIDC SSO must be configured before SCIM; listed prerequisites are the Enterprise package and verified domains only.
SCIM base URL pattern is not documented (the domains API only exposes a read-only scim_base_url field per verified domain).
SCIM token expiry is not documented.
Supported SCIM endpoints beyond Users/Groups (ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas, ResourceTypes, Bulk), filtering, pagination, PUT vs PATCH, delete and reactivate behaviour are not documented.
Supported SCIM user and group attributes are not documented (only that email is the likely unique identifier in Okta).
Whether SCIM deactivation revokes active sessions or personal API keys, and what data is retained, is not documented.

Whether the REST user-management API (members, invites, roles) is available on the Free plan or gated is not stated; role endpoints are presumably tied to RBAC on Enterprise but this is not stated per endpoint.

Which plan unlocks the activity log API is not stated; platform packages list activity log retention of 7 days (Boost), 2 months (Scale), 60 months (Enterprise), and querying via PostHog AI needs Scale or Enterprise.

Microsoft Entra gallery, Google Workspace and JumpCloud catalogue listings for PostHog could not be confirmed (guessed Entra tutorial URL 404; JumpCloud returned 403). The Okta OIN catalogue search returns no PostHog app (c49); PostHog's own Okta guide uses a custom app integration.

OneLogin catalogue page could not be loaded (bot protection); whether the prebuilt OneLogin PostHog app supports provisioning is unknown — PostHog's SCIM guide uses OneLogin's generic 'SCIM Provisioner with SAML' connector instead.
